global_issues.title: US flags Korea and others as China chip tariff evasion routes
global_issues.note: Confirmed and actually broader than stated: White House 'Great Transshipment Scam' report names 40+ countries (incl. South Korea's Gyeonggi chip belt, Japan, EU) as transshipment risks, estimating up to $303B/yr in evaded tariffs. Taiwan's proposed tougher AI chip export rules (targeting rerouted Nvidia-powered servers to China) are also independently confirmed and still current.

global_issues.title: Soft retail sales and flat PPI push yields up, cut Fed hike odds
global_issues.note: Confirmed: July retail sales fell 0.6% m/m (biggest drop in over a year, missed expectations), July PPI flat m/m. Reduces case for a September Fed hike. Consistent with reporting from WaPo, TradingKey, Reuters.

missing_major_news.title: Broadcom (AVGO) shares fell ~5% on a VMware vCenter security vulnerability (CVE-2026-59310) being actively exploited, plus AI-valuation concerns ahead of earnings
missing_major_news.impact: Not in the watchlist directly, but material to the semiconductor/AI-chip complex the briefing already frames as under pressure (NVDA, TSM, MU); a 5% drop in a major AI bellwether on the same day is a notable sector signal that's missing from the sector analysis.

market_mood_check.note: The 'green/98.1' bullish score and MU-surge headline are accurate in isolation, but the briefing omits that the broader market actually fell on Aug 14 (S&P, Nasdaq, Dow all down) on weak UMich consumer sentiment — a materially bearish, not bullish, cross-current for the same session. Calling the mood unambiguously 'green' without noting this broader pullback overstates bullishness.

grok_report.summary: The two global macro items (Korea/chip tariff transshipment report, soft retail sales/PPI) are accurate and well-sourced, though the briefing understates how sweeping the transshipment report was (40+ countries). The bigger issue is the market mood assessment: it ignores the weak University of Michigan consumer sentiment print that actually pulled the S&P, Nasdaq, and Dow lower on Aug 14, making the 'green/98.1' bullish framing incomplete. TSM's reported price/direction also looks off versus available quotes.
